chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin 'Isa, from Qasim bin Yahya, from his grandfather, Hasan bin Rashid, from Abdullah bin Sinan, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, who said:

I asked him about «Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Raheem», so he, peace be upon him, said: The Baa' is the Magnificence of Allah, the Seen is the Sublimity of Allah, and the Miim is the Nobility of Allah – and some narrated: the Kingdom of Allah – and Allah is the God of everything, and the Merciful to all in the world, and the Merciful in particular to the believers.

key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: The Basmala, the opening invocation of Quranic chapters

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the letters in Bismillah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* offers a unique Isma'ili-influenced or early Shia esoteric interpretation where the letters B, S, and M in 'Bismillah' are decoded as divine attributes (Sublimity, Magnificence, and Kingdom/Majesty). It further clarifies the theological distinction between 'Ar-Rahman' (universal mercy for all creation) and 'Ar-Raheem' (specific, enduring mercy for the believers), a nuance often discussed in Shia tafsir to explain the dual nature of divine compassion.
